description:
Unix timestamp parameters passed by callers are named inconsistently across the store methods:

- ChatStore::create(&self, chat_id, kind, contact_id, now_unix: i64)  — crates/kith-store/src/chat.rs line 229
- ContactStore::upsert(&self, peer_user_id, peer_login, peer_mailbox_host, display_name, now_unix: i64)  — crates/kith-store/src/contact.rs line 38
- SpaceStore::create_space(&self, ..., created_at_unix: i64)  — crates/kith-store/src/space.rs line 194
- SpaceStore::add_member(&self, space_id, user_id, nick, joined_at_unix: i64, role_ids)  — crates/kith-store/src/space.rs line 772
- MessageStore::insert(&self, ..., created_at_unix: i64, ...)  — crates/kith-store/src/message.rs line 959

'now_unix' (chat, contact) and 'created_at_unix' (space, message) both mean a caller-supplied current Unix timestamp in seconds, but they use different names. 'joined_at_unix' is unique to space members.

Fix: standardize on 'now_unix' for the 'current wall-clock time' parameter across all stores, and reserve 'created_at_unix'/'joined_at_unix' only when the timestamp represents something domain-specific that differs from now (e.g., a backfilled or peer-supplied timestamp).
title: Timestamp parameter named now_unix in some stores, created_at_unix/joined_at_unix in others
